  "text": "The library kept its spare chairs in a cupboard behind the atlases. On Tuesdays, Martin brought six out for the reading group, though only five people came.

He put the sixth beside the radiator.

Mrs Bell arrived first, carrying a book wrapped in a supermarket bag. She never used the self-service machine.

“It doesn’t like me,” she said.

“It needs the barcode facing down.”

“Yes. You’ve mentioned.”

He renewed her book.

In November, she asked whether the library had anything about repairing wooden boats.

“Large boats?”

“About this big.”

She held her hands apart, then moved them closer together.

He found a book in the basement. Its borrowing slip was stamped with dates from before he had worked there.

The following Tuesday, she showed him a photograph on her phone. A small boat lay upside down on newspaper.

“My husband started it.”

Martin enlarged the photograph with two fingers.

“Those might be clamps you need.”

“I’ve got his clamps.”

After Christmas, she missed three meetings. Martin returned the extra chair to the cupboard, then brought it out again when the others arrived.

In February, Mrs Bell came in with a cardboard box.

The boat had a blue hull and a narrow white stripe. One end of the stripe wandered slightly.

“The tape lifted,” she said.

“Have you tried it on water?”

“The bath. It lists.”

She set it on the returns desk while she took off her gloves.

Martin fetched the repair book.

“I’ve finished with that,” she said.

He opened it to the chapter on ballast.

Outside, rain struck the windows. Mrs Bell pulled the sixth chair up to the desk."
